_comment: Boot-log signature database for the MT6768 / A31 porting kit. triage-bootlog.py scans a kernel log against these. 'severity': fatal = boot-blocking; intentional = deliberate, not a bug; warning = non-fatal but real; info = harmless/marker. 'fallback': true = a generic/collateral signature that is SUPPRESSED when a more specific cause is already identified (near a specific explainer, or anywhere once a non-fallback fatal is present) - keeps teardown noise and generic catchers from masquerading as the root cause. 'correlations' escalate a combination: when all listed ids fire in one log, the note is raised in the verdict. 'fix' points to a crash-database section or patch; it is "" when the problem is an old-kernel-vs-new-Android capability gap with NO source patch (the real fix is a newer kernel base). The triage NEVER invents a patch; for an unknown fatal it only flags that a human/AI must read the trace. Add new signatures as you find them.

correlations.note: ROOT CAUSE = init::SetupSelinux() aborted while a REMOVED logical partition (e.g. product) is still listed in fstab/dynamic_partitions_info, so init still queries it via device-mapper, gets 'DM_DEV_STATUS failed for <partition>: No such device or address', and the split-sepolicy load that follows cannot find that partition's sepolicy/file_contexts/property_contexts pieces. InitAborter() kills PID1, the kernel cannot survive PID1 dying, and (on this platform) that panic is caught by Samsung's sec_debug/WDT path which forces sec_reboot(0, 'bootloader') - landing on a device with only fastbootd (no real interactive bootloader) in a hard bootloop with no easy way out. Deleting the partition image is NOT enough - every reference to it (fstab.<chip>, dynamic_partitions_info.txt / misc_info, the sepolicy manifest) must be removed together, or SetupSelinux keeps expecting files that no longer exist. This is independent of enforcing vs permissive: permissive only skips ENFORCING denials from an already-loaded policy, it does not help if the policy cannot be LOADED/merged at all.

ROOT CAUSE = the kernel eBPF gap. netbpfload could not load the tethering BPF programs AND the bpfloader init service (reboot_on_failure) force-rebooted the device (reboot,bpfloader-failed). The old 4.14 kernel lacks BPF features this Android build's bpfloader requires, so the device bootloops every boot. Real fix: a newer kernel base (5.10+ GKI). Stopgap only: remove 'reboot_on_failure' from the bpfloader init .rc so a BPF failure degrades networking instead of bricking boot (that is how the working 4.14 ROM tolerates the identical warning).
The system_server ClatCoordinator SIGABRT is the user-space face of the SAME missing clat (464XLAT) BPF maps - a symptom of the eBPF gap, not an independent bug.

signatures.name: bpfloader reboot_on_failure bootloop
signatures.meaning: THE boot-ending event. netbpfload failed to load the tethering eBPF programs, the bpfloader init service exited (status 38 after a ~20s wait), and because it is declared reboot_on_failure, init issued shutdown_command 'reboot,bpfloader-failed' -> HandlePowerctlMessage -> sec_reboot. The device bootloops every boot. Root cause: the 4.14 A31 kernel lacks BPF features the newer Android tethering APEX requires. This literal appears only at the real reboot decision, never on a healthy boot.
signatures.action: No source patch - old-kernel vs new-Android capability gap. Real fix: move to a newer kernel base (5.10+ GKI) with the BPF features the tethering APEX needs. Stopgap: remove 'reboot_on_failure' from the bpfloader init .rc so a BPF load failure degrades networking instead of bricking boot.

signatures.name: system_server ClatCoordinator SIGABRT
signatures.meaning: system_server aborts (SIGABRT) during ClatCoordinator JNI registration (libservice-connectivity.so, via NetworkStatsServiceInitializer), repeating across zygote re-forks. This is the USER-SPACE SYMPTOM of the eBPF gap - the clat 464XLAT BPF maps never loaded - not the device-ending event itself (that is the init bpfloader reboot). The symbol appears only inside tombstone backtraces, so it is self-validating.
signatures.action: Downstream of the BPF load failure, not an independent root cause - resolved by fixing the bpfloader/kernel BPF gap (see bpfloader-reboot).

signatures.name: gpufreq NULL deref reading the GPU efuse
signatures.meaning: MTK gpufreq called nvmem_cell_get('efuse_segment_cell') but the A31 DT has no such nvmem cell, then dereferenced the ERR_PTR. Dies ~1.0s.
signatures.action: Apply the get_devinfo_with_index(30) & 0xFF fallback. Every MTK driver reading an efuse via nvmem on this device needs the same fallback.

signatures.name: EINT controller not found (no GPIO interrupts)
signatures.meaning: mtk_build_eint() looked up the EINT controller by node name 'eint' but on the A31 it is named apirq@1000b000, so hw->eint stays NULL and the first driver to request a GPIO IRQ dies. Without EINT nothing with a GPIO interrupt works (touch, buttons, sensors, SIM/USB detect).
signatures.action: Resolve the EINT base through the reg_base_eint phandle first, then fall back to of_find_node_by_name(NULL, 'eint').

signatures.name: thermal sysrst cooler BUG() on a bogus trip
signatures.meaning: The mtktsAP-sysrst cooler calls BUG() as a 'thermal protection reset' when its zone crosses a trip at init. The AP NTC (BTS, thermistor-ch*) is mis-mapped/mis-calibrated on this port, reports an impossible temperature, the trip fires immediately, and the SoC reboots. Dies ~1.1s.
signatures.action: Not yet fixed in-tree. Either correct the io-channels/thermistor-ch* auxadc mapping for the A31, or make set_cur_state log-and-return instead of BUG() on a clearly bogus init-time trip.

signatures.name: init SetupSelinux() abort (InitAborter) - policy LOAD failure, not an enforcement denial
signatures.meaning: init's SetupSelinux() called InitAborter() and PID1 died. This fires during POLICY LOAD/MERGE, before enforcement even matters - a permissive kernel (androidboot.selinux=permissive) does NOT protect against this, because permissive only skips enforcing denials from a policy that already loaded; it cannot load a policy that fails to merge/parse at all. Usual causes on a GSI-on-older-vendor port: (1) a plat_sepolicy_vers.txt / sepolicy_version mismatch between the vendor's declared platform API level and the mapping .cil files the system/GSI ships (same class of bug as the A31 plat_sepolicy_vers 31-vs-30 fix, just a different pair of versions); (2) the split-sepolicy loader still expecting pieces (sepolicy/file_contexts/property_contexts) from a partition that was removed but not fully de-listed from fstab/dynamic_partitions_info - see the stale-partition-dm-status correlation when both fire together.
signatures.action: Diff the vendor's /vendor/etc/selinux/plat_sepolicy_vers.txt against the mapping .cil files under /system/etc/selinux/mapping/ on the GSI - the vendor's declared version must have a matching mapping file on the system side. Then grep the vendor/system fstab and dynamic_partitions_info/misc_info for every removed partition (e.g. product) and delete all references, not just the partition image, and recompile/repackage the merged sepolicy (precompiled_sepolicy) afterward so it no longer expects files from a partition that is gone.

signatures.name: DM_DEV_STATUS failed for a removed logical partition
signatures.regex: DM_DEV_STATUS failed for (\w+): No such device or address
signatures.meaning: init tried to query a logical (dynamic) partition via device-mapper and it does not exist. By itself this is often tolerated (init just logs 'Could not update logical partition' and moves on) - it only becomes the root cause when it is immediately followed by a selinux-setup-abort in the SAME boot (see that correlation), meaning something still expects files that lived on the now-removed partition.
signatures.action: Confirm every fstab entry, dynamic_partitions_info/misc_info reference AND the sepolicy manifest for the named partition were removed together with the partition image itself - not just the image.

signatures.name: init force-reboot (reboot-reason catcher)
signatures.regex: Got shutdown_command '|####Reboot start, reason:|reboot: Restarting system with command |sec_reboot \(
signatures.meaning: Generic high-signal catcher: init received a powerctl shutdown/reboot command and restarted the system; the reboot reason/target names the culprit. Keyed on the reboot-reason lines (one per real reboot), NOT the per-service "has 'reboot_on_failure' option and failed" string, which over-matches and would mis-name a teardown victim (e.g. vold) as the cause. Suppressed once a specific cause (e.g. bpfloader-reboot) is already identified; it is the fallback that names the reason when no specific signature matched.
signatures.action: Read the reboot reason/target to identify the failing service, then triage that service.

signatures.name: Kernel panic - not syncing
signatures.regex: Kernel panic - not syncing|Unable to handle kernel (NULL pointer|paging request)|Internal error: Oops
signatures.meaning: A genuine fatal fault - but only counts if NOT already explained by a more specific signature (e.g. the deliberate forced reset's Oops, or a named crash above).
signatures.action: Read the pc:/lr: and Call trace lines, match the faulting function to the driver source (unpack Image via tools/a31_bootimg.py + gunzip), and add a new signature here with the fix once known. The triage will not invent a patch for an unknown fault - this is the point where a human or an AI reads the trace.

signatures.name: Deliberate forced reset (not a crash)
signatures.meaning: Samsung's forced-upload/ramdump hook fired because Volume-Down + Power were held - a deliberate BUG() at sec_hard_reset_hook.c:131, NOT a spontaneous kernel bug. If this is the only BUG() in the log, the kernel did not crash on its own (the surrounding log shows a healthy boot). A generic Oops on the same line is suppressed so it does not masquerade as a real crash.
signatures.action: Ignore. If you were hunting a boot crash, re-capture WITHOUT holding the keys - this event is you forcing the reset.

signatures.name: netbpfload CRITICAL FAILURE loading BPF
signatures.meaning: netbpfload could not load the tethering/netd eBPF programs on this kernel. SURVIVABLE on its own - the working 4.14 ROM emits the identical line and still boots. It becomes FATAL only when the SAME boot also shows 'reboot,bpfloader-failed' (bpfloader is reboot_on_failure): see the correlation note. The old 'failed to load: -' regex was wrong - it matched the surviving netd.o case and MISSED the dead 'non-optional program ... failed to load' case, i.e. it flagged the healthy boot and missed the bootlooping one; now keyed on the CRITICAL-FAILURE banner.
signatures.action: Root fix is the kernel BPF gap - a newer kernel base (5.10+ GKI). Informational by itself; fatal only when paired with bpfloader-reboot in the same boot.

signatures.name: MTK/Samsung vendor audio HAL SIGSEGV
signatures.meaning: Vendor audio HAL (/vendor/bin/hw/android.hardware.audio.service.mediatek) SIGSEGV null-pointer deref in adev_set_parameters, via sec_dev_set_parameters / SehDevice::setParameters - a vendor audio blob mismatched against the A31 (MT6768) platform (e.g. an A34/A32 vendor on A31). A restartable HAL crash; breaks audio, NOT boot-fatal. The regex binds library+symbol on the crash frame so it cannot fire on a benign HAL-load line that merely names the .so.
signatures.action: No source patch - vendor .so mismatch. Use the A31's own matching audio.primary.mt6768.so / Samsung sec audio HAL, or rebuild the vendor audio HAL against A31.

signatures.name: Trustonic/MobiCore TEE tee_mmu_create WARNING
signatures.meaning: Non-fatal WARN_ON in the MediaTek MobiCore/Trustonic TEE driver's tee_mmu_create during keymaster/vaultkeeper init. Warn-and-continue - the TEE session still opens.
signatures.action: Related to the TEE 410 gfp/serialisation patch. Safe to ignore for boot; tighten only if keymaster/vaultkeeper actually fail.

signatures.name: RPMB write-counter mismatch (keymaster/vaultkeeper)
signatures.meaning: The TEE's RPMB replay-protected block read saw a write-counter mismatch and retried. Usually a transient at first boot after an RPMB/userdata change; keymaster recovers. Persistent mismatches can mean the RPMB key is not provisioned for this ROM.
signatures.action: Ignore if boot continues and keystore works. If it loops, the RPMB key state does not match the ROM - a vendor/keymaster concern, not a kernel patch.

signatures.name: exFAT / sdfat SD-card mount issue
signatures.meaning: SD-card exFAT mount path. On this device sdfat mis-parsed time_offset for exFAT.
signatures.action: See the 1-byte sdfat Image patch that repoints the time_offset token.

signatures.name: init service exit timeout / hang
signatures.meaning: An init service hung and exited after a long wait (e.g. 'Service bpfloader (pid 998) exited with status 38 waiting took 20.035 seconds'). This long-wait line is often the proximate trigger just before a reboot_on_failure reboot. Suppressed once a specific fatal cause is identified.
signatures.action: Inspect the named service and its exit status. Non-fatal by itself unless that service is reboot_on_failure.

signatures.name: apexd flush_work WARN during reboot teardown
signatures.meaning: Non-fatal flush_work WARN_ON, repeated many times, while apexd unmounts APEX dm-verity/loop devices DURING an already-committed reboot teardown. Shutdown collateral and log noise, not a cause.
signatures.action: Ignore for boot triage - symptom of the in-progress reboot.

signatures.name: capability 'PERFMON' not supported by the kernel
signatures.regex: capability 'PERFMON' not supported by the kernel
signatures.meaning: An APEX init.rc asked for the PERFMON capability, which this older kernel does not define. Harmless - init just skips it.
signatures.action: No action. Cosmetic on a pre-5.8 kernel.

signatures.name: netbpfload unprivileged_bpf_disabled sysctl touch
signatures.meaning: netbpfload touching the unprivileged_bpf_disabled sysctl - a marker of the newer-Android-netbpfload vs older-kernel BPF-interface gap. Present on BOTH the bootlooping and the working boot, so benign by itself.
signatures.action: Informational marker of the kernel/userspace BPF interface gap; resolved by the same newer-kernel fix as the BPF load failures.

signatures.name: Service death during reboot teardown (collateral)
signatures.regex: Service 'mobicore' \(pid [0-9]+\) received SIGABRT|Service vold has 'reboot_on_failure' option and failed
signatures.meaning: Services dying AFTER the reboot was already decided, as init tears down all services (e.g. mobicore SIGABRT, vold SIGKILL). Collateral of the already-committed reboot, NOT independent causes. This is the vold line the naive 'reboot_on_failure ... failed' regex wrongly promoted to a culprit.
signatures.action: Suppressed whenever a reboot reason (bpfloader-reboot) is already present earlier in the same boot. Do not count as separate boot-fatal faults.
